history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration request entities to monitor consultant expenditure funded through all resources, including the regular budget, other assessed and extrabudgetary resources, strengthen long-term capability-building of internal staff and gradually reduce the reliance on consultants.
history.administration_response: As indicated by the General Assembly, the primary consideration for the allocation of resources is the efficient and effective implementation of mandates. In formulating budget proposals, programme managers are required to balance the need to implement mandates in an efficient and effective manner, and to use realistic assumptions that factor in past trends in their budget proposals (A/72/5 (Vol. I), chap. II, para. 324). The Controller issued a memorandum to heads of entity (as mentioned in previous responses) requesting the close monitoring of expenditures in the light of expenditure trends. The Administration will continue to monitor expenditures under consultants. Material variances at the section level or budget class level will be justified in the context of the financial performance report, in accordance with the established practice. The Administration requests the closure of this recommendation.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Administration stressed the importance of monitoring consultant expenditures by sending a memorandum on budget implementation to heads of entity and made notable efforts to monitor the use of delegated authority, the Board considers this recommendation implemented.
